mainTopic: Is the blood of a נבילה (an animal that died without proper שחיטה) טמא? The question is resolved through the ruling of רבי יהודה. Then a new משנה begins about how much wine one may pledge as a נסכים offering.
overview: The amud opens as רבי ביבי explains that his mind is too unsettled to rule on whether the blood of a נבילה is טמא. רב יוסף answers that רבי יהודה, the decisor of the נשיא's household, ruled by his own tradition. That tradition says בית הלל, unusually the stricter side here, hold that such blood is טמא. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds that this applies only to a רביעית, since that much blood can harden into a כזית. A new משנה then teaches that one may pledge 3, 4, 6, or more לוג of wine for נסכים, but not 1, 2, or 5. The גמרא asks whether there is a קבע for נסכים, using the case of someone who brings 5 לוג. אביי's proof from the six collection horns is rejected. רבא proves from a ברייתא that there is no קבע, and רב אשי's challenge from the משנה is answered. Finally אביי begins a new question: if there is a קבע, what is the law for eleven לוג? That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ביבי explains why he cannot answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי ביבי ends his reply by saying that 'that man' (he himself) relies on a baker for bread, so his mind is not settled enough to decide the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that man (meaning: I) relies on a baker.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an earlier story. רבי ביבי explains that he cannot answer the question about the blood of a נבילה because his life is too unsettled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who has to buy his bread from a baker each day lives with worry about his livelihood. רבי ביבי is saying he lacks the calm, clear mind needed to give a הוראה. He gives no ruling, so the next step asks what the conclusion was, and step 3 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That man.' A polite way of saying 'I.'
A baker or bread-seller.
Relies on, depends on.

steps.confusionAlert: 'That man' is not some other person. It is רבי ביבי speaking about himself in a modest, indirect way.

phrases.english: And that man
phrases.notes: This is a humble way of saying 'I.' רבי ביבי is talking about himself.

phrases.english: relies on a baker.
phrases.notes: He means he has to buy his bread every day, so his mind isn't calm enough to rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from the previous daf, in which רבי ביבי was asked about the blood of a נבילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No real answer. He explains that he is not in a settled state to rule.

steps.title: What was the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי ביבי did not answer, the גמרא asks what the conclusion on this question was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final decision was about the blood of a נבילה. This is a setup line that prepares for רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story ended without a ruling. Now the גמרא steps outside the story to ask for the actual הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What was [concluded] about it?' A request for the final outcome of a question.

phrases.english: What was [concluded] about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the question that רבי ביבי left unanswered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling on whether the blood of a נבילה is טמא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה ruled for the נשיא's household
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that רבי יהודה was the הוראה-giver of the נשיא's household, and he ruled according to his own tradition, which holds that the blood is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי יהודה was the decisor of the house of the נשיא, and he instructed them according to his tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. רבי יהודה, the official decisor for the נשיא's house, ruled on it based on what he had learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his tradition' (שמעתיה) point to רבי יהודה's own teaching. The next step quotes that teaching, which shows that the blood of a נבילה is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The halachic decisor, the one who gives הוראה.
The household of the נשיא.
According to his own tradition or teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוֹרְיָינָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was the decisor of the house of the Nasi,
and he instructed him according to his tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מוֹרְיָינָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה ruled by his own tradition that the blood of a נבילה is טמא.

steps.title: Source for רבי יהודה's tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה lists six cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict. One of them is the blood of a נבילה, which בית שמאי call טהור and בית הלל call טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says, six things are among the leniencies of בית שמאי and the stringencies of בית הלל. The blood of נבילות: בית שמאי declare it טהור, and בית הלל declare it טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows what 'his tradition' was. רבי יהודה reports that בית הלל hold the blood of a נבילה is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually בית הלל are the more lenient side, so this is one of a special list where they are stricter. Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, רבי יהודה ruled that the blood is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Cases where בית שמאי are lenient.
Cases where בית הלל are strict.
The blood of animals that died without proper שחיטה.
Declare טהור (pure) / declare טמא (impure).

steps.confusionAlert: Normally בית הלל are the lenient ones. This list is unusual because in these six cases בית הלל are the stricter side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the practical ruling: we follow בית הלל, so the blood of a נבילה is טמא.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
six things are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai
and among the stringencies of Beit Hillel.
The blood of carcasses:
Beit Shammai declare it pure,
and Beit Hillel declare it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for 'his tradition' mentioned in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's tradition holds the blood of a נבילה is טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's list of six leniencies of בית שמאי and stringencies of בית הלל.

steps.title: Only a רביעית of blood is טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה limits בית הלל's ruling: the blood is טמא only in the amount of a רביעית, because that much blood could harden into a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: even when בית הלל declared it טמא, they did so only for a רביעית, since it could congeal and make up a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: A son of רבי יהודה adds a limit to בית הלל's ruling. The blood is טמא only if there is at least a רביעית of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flesh of a נבילה is טמא in the amount of a כזית. A רביעית of liquid blood, once it hardens, would be about a כזית. So that is the smallest amount of blood that can be treated like the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a standard liquid measure.
To congeal, to harden.
An olive's size, the minimum amount of נבילה flesh that is טמא.
Since, because.

steps.whatToRemember: The blood of a נבילה is טמא according to בית הלל, but only in an amount of a רביעית, since that much blood can harden into a כזית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even when Beit Hillel declared it impure,
they declared it impure only in a quarter-log,
since it could congeal
and amount to an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַף כְּשֶׁטִּמְּאוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies בית הלל's ruling from step 4 by adding a minimum amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood of a נבילה is טמא only in the amount of a רביעית, which could harden into a כזית.

steps.title: Which amounts of wine may be pledged
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: one may not pledge 1, 2, or 5 לוג of wine as נסכים, but one may pledge 3, 4, 6, or any amount above 6.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One does not pledge a לוג, two, or five. But one pledges three, four, six, and from six and up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches which amounts of wine a person may pledge as a נדבה of נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine נסכים come in set amounts: 3 לוג with a lamb, 4 with a ram, and 6 with a bull. A pledge must match one of these amounts. Any amount above 6 can be built from combinations of them, so it is allowed, but 1, 2, and 5 match nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה.'
Pledge as a voluntary offering (נדבה).
A liquid measure, about the volume of six eggs.
Above, more than that.

steps.confusionAlert: Five is not allowed even though it falls between 4 and 6. It does not match any set amount, and it cannot be made from 3, 4, or 6.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One does not pledge one log, two, or five,
phrases.notes: This is talking about pledging wine for נסכים.

phrases.english: but one pledges three, four, or six,
and from six and up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the blood of a נבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine for נסכים may be pledged only in amounts of 3, 4, 6, or more than 6 לוג, not 1, 2, or 5.

steps.title: Is a pledged amount of libation wine one fixed unit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is a קבע for נסכים, meaning the amount pledged must stay as one unit, or whether it may be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: חכמים asked: Is there a fixed amount for libations, or is there no fixed amount for libations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question that the משנה left unanswered: once a person brings a certain amount of wine for נסכים, must it be offered as one fixed unit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed which amounts can be pledged, but it did not say what happens to an amount that does not match any standard measure. The question is whether the wine is locked in as one unit (יש קבע) or can be broken into smaller valid parts (אין קבע). The next step explains what case this is about.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question the גמרא tries to settle)
A fixed set amount that cannot be divided
Wine libations poured on the מזבח

phrases.english: Gemara:
A dilemma was raised before them:
Is there a fixed amount for libations,
or is there no fixed amount for libations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה about pledging amounts of wine for נסכים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pledged amount of libation wine must be offered as one undivided unit.

steps.title: The practical case: someone brings five לוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the case: 5 לוג. Without a fixed amount, 4 go to a ram's נסכים and 1 goes to נדבה. With a fixed amount, nothing is offered until he adds more wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Where he brought five. If you say there is no fixed amount, he takes four of them and offers them, since that fits a ram, and the extra one becomes a gift offering. But if you say there is a fixed amount, they are not offered until he fills them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks itself what case the question is about. It answers with a person who brings 5 לוג and shows how each side of the question would rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 5 לוג does not match any standard measure. If there is no קבע, you split it: 4 לוג are used for a ram, and the leftover 1 לוג goes to נדבה. If there is a קבע, the 5 stay together, and nothing can be offered until he adds wine to reach a valid amount.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (asks for the exact situation)
Ram (a sacrifice whose נסכים are 4 לוג of wine)
Gift offering. Here it means extra funds used for communal gift offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'no fixed amount' means any amount can be offered. It means the wine can be split into valid standard portions, and the leftover goes to נדבה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
For example, where he brought five.
phrases.notes: Five לוג of wine. That amount does not match any standard measure.

phrases.english: If you say there is no fixed amount for libations,
he takes four of them and offers them,
since those are suitable for a ram,
and the other one becomes a gift offering.
But if you say there is a fixed amount for libations,
they are not offered until he adds to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical case where the question of step 7 makes a difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does it matter whether there is a קבע for נסכים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 5 לוג: either split into 4 for a ram and 1 for נדבה, or left unoffered until more wine is added.

steps.title: אביי brings the six horns for נדבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a proof from the teaching that there were six collection horns for נדבה, one for each kind of leftover money.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? אביי said: Come and hear: There were six horns for gift offerings. And we asked: What were they for? For leftover money from sin offerings, from guilt offerings, from a נזיר's guilt offering, from a מצורע's guilt offering, from pairs of birds, and from the meal offering of a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the answer, and אביי sets up a proof. He quotes the list of the six horns for נדבה. This step lays the groundwork, and the punch line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each horn matched one specific kind of leftover money, and that money was used for communal gift offerings. The list is closed at six, and leftover נסכים are not on it. אביי will use this missing item as his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover funds set aside for a sacrifice but not used
Pairs of bird offerings
The meal offering a poor sinner brings in place of an animal

phrases.english: What is the answer?
Abaye said: Come and hear:
Six for gift offerings,
phrases.notes: Six collection horns in the מקדש, from משנה שקלים 6:5.

phrases.english: and we asked: What were they for?
For leftover money from sin offerings,
and leftover money from guilt offerings,
and leftover money from a nazirite's guilt offering,
and leftover money from a leper's guilt offering,
and leftover money from pairs of birds,
and leftover money from a sinner's meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of steps 7 and 8 using an outside source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is a קבע for נסכים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that there were six horns for נדבה, each matched to a specific kind of leftover money.

steps.title: No horn for leftover libations, so there is a fixed amount
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes his proof: if there were no fixed amount, they should have set up another horn for leftover נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, let them set up another horn for leftover libations!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the punch line of his proof. If leftover wine could go to נדבה, there should be a seventh horn for it, and there isn't one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there were no קבע, the extra 1 לוג out of 5 would become נדבה, and leftover money from נסכים would need its own collection horn. Since only six horns are listed, there is no such leftover. That suggests there is a קבע for נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (sets up a logical challenge)
A horn-shaped collection box in the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof: only six horns for נדבה existed and none was for leftover נסכים, which would suggest there is a קבע. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first attempt to settle the question, using how the מקדש's donation system was set up.

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If it were true that there is no fixed amount, so the extra wine goes to נדבה.

phrases.english: let them set up another horn
for leftover libations!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's proof begun in step 9 by pointing out what is missing from the list.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a קבע for נסכים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: No seventh horn existed for leftover נסכים, so splitting the wine never produced leftovers.

steps.title: Why there was no horn for leftover wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof. The six horns were for money going to communal נדבה offerings. Leftover wine is common, so one person's leftover can be joined with another's and offered right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those horns were for money that goes to communal gift offerings. But leftover libation wine is common. One person's leftover can be combined with another person's leftover, and it is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof. A missing horn does not prove that נסכים have a fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that if נסכים had no fixed amount, there should have been a horn for the leftover wine. The answer is that no horn is needed, because leftovers from different people can be combined into a full amount and offered immediately. So the missing horn proves nothing, and רבא tries a new proof in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal gift offerings, paid for from the public fund
They are common, found often
They combine, join together
They are offered

phrases.english: Those go to communal gift offerings;
phrases.notes: "Those" means the six horns from אביי's proof.

phrases.english: these are common;
phrases.notes: "These" means the leftover לוגין of נסכים wine.

phrases.english: it is possible that they combine,
this person's and that person's together,
and they are offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ לְנִדְבַת צִבּוּר אָזְלִי, הָנֵי שְׁכִיחִי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the six horns.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The missing horn can be explained another way. Leftover wine is common and gets combined and offered at once, so it never needs to be stored.

steps.title: רבא quotes a ברייתא on pledged נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: one may pledge נסכים on their own, the minimum is 3 לוג, one may add more, and one may not give less.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. "Home born" teaches that one may pledge libations. How much? Three לוג. How do we know that if he wants to add, he may add? The verse says "shall be." Could he give less? The verse says "in this manner."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new proof by quoting a ברייתא. Its key word is "add," and the next step will examine that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a floor of 3 לוג, the amount used for a lamb. It also says one may go above that floor. The question of whether נסכים have a fixed amount will depend on what kind of adding is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Home born, a word from the פסוק used to teach this law
One may pledge as a voluntary gift
A unit of liquid measure
The verse teaches, the source in the פסוק
One might think, opening a possibility the ברייתא will reject

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
"Home born" teaches that one may pledge libations,
And how much? Three log.
And from where do we know that if he wants to add, he may add?
The verse says: "shall be."
Could he give less?
The verse says: "in this manner."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:13, the same פסוק as "home born."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's proof was rejected, רבא tries a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: That there is no fixed amount for נסכים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns from פסוקים that one may pledge נסכים, starting at 3 לוג, and may add more.

steps.title: Adding cannot mean only 4 or 6
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what "add" means. If it meant 4 or 6 לוג, there would be no need for a special source, because those amounts fit a ram and a bull just as 3 fits a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "he may add" mean? If you say four or six, what is special about three? That it fits a lamb? Four and six also fit a ram and a bull!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reading the ברייתא closely and ruling out one meaning of "add." This sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוג is allowed because it is the amount for a lamb. Four is the amount for a ram and six for a bull, so they would be allowed for the same reason. A separate source for "adding" must therefore be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, offering a possible reading the גמרא will reject
What is the difference?
They are fit, suitable
Lamb (its נסכים are 3 לוג)
Ram (its נסכים are 4 לוג)
Bull (its נסכים are 6 לוג)

phrases.english: What does "he may add" mean?
If you say four or six,
what is different about three?
phrases.notes: He means: why would three come from one source and four or six need a separate one?

phrases.english: Because it fits a lamb?

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה וְשִׁשָּׁה נָמֵי חֲזוּ לְאַיִל וּפַר!
phrases.english: Four and six also fit a ram and a bull!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the word "add" in רבא's ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which amounts the word "add" in the ברייתא allows.

steps.title: Adding means five: no fixed amount
steps.stepSummary: Since "add" cannot mean 4 or 6, it must mean 5 לוג. This proves there is no fixed amount for נסכים, and the גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean five? Learn from this that there is no fixed amount for libations. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that "add" refers to 5 לוג. This answers the question from Step 7: נסכים have no fixed amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five לוג does not match the נסכים of any animal, yet the ברייתא allows it. That only works if 5 can be split, for example 4 for a ram and 1 as a נדבה. So the pledged amount does not have to stay as one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that... (moving to the only remaining reading)
There is no fixed amount for libations, so the amount can be divided
Learn from it, a proof that the גמרא accepts

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling is אין קבע לנסכים. A pledge of 5 לוג works: 4 go to a ram's נסכים and 1 goes to נדבה. The proof is that the ברייתא's word "add" must refer to 5.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean five?
And learn from this that there is no fixed amount for libations.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, חֲמִשָּׁה, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֵין קֶבַע לִנְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's proof by settling on the one reading left over.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no fixed amount for נסכים. Five לוג is valid and is divided between a ram's נסכים and a נדבה.

steps.title: רב אשי brings a proof from the משנה that five לוג is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the משנה that one may not donate one, two, or five לוג. Because five is listed with two, five must be just as unusable. That would mean there is a fixed amount for נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Didn't we already learn this in the משנה? One may not donate a לוג, two, or five. The משנה puts five next to two. Just as two is not usable at all, five is also not usable at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back against the conclusion we just reached. He quotes a משנה that seems to show five לוג cannot be donated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step proved from a ברייתא that five לוג may be donated, so there is no fixed amount. רב אשי points out that the משנה lists five together with two. Two לוג fits no offering at all, so the משנה seems to be saying five is just as useless. That supports the view that there is a fixed amount.

steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing one, two, and five לוג together as amounts that may not be donated
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of step 14 that there is no fixed amount for נסכים (אין קבע לנסכים).

steps.title: The comparison between two and five is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that listing two and five together does not make them the same. Each one is forbidden for its own reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real proof? This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב אשי's proof. Just because two amounts appear in the same list does not mean they share the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumed that five is unusable in the same way as two. The גמרא says each case stands on its own. Two לוג fits no offering at all, but five can still be used, since part of it matches a real offering. So the משנה does not prove there is a fixed amount, and the conclusion of step 14 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a real comparison? A way of rejecting a proof drawn from two cases being listed together
this one is as it is, and that one is as it is; each case has its own reason

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof by denying that the two listed cases share a reason
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison between two and five, not the משנה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being listed together in the משנה does not mean two amounts are forbidden for the same reason
steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion stands: there is no fixed amount for נסכים. The משנה's list does not prove otherwise, because two and five are forbidden for different reasons.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two and five are listed together but for different reasons: two fits no offering, while five can be split (four for a ram, one for נדבה). So the משנה does not contradict אין קבע לנסכים.

steps.title: אביי sets up a question about eleven לוג if there is a fixed amount
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if there is no fixed amount, there is nothing to ask. If there is a fixed amount, amounts up to ten לוג are clear to him. He begins to ask about eleven.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If you say there is no fixed amount for נסכים, then there is no fixed amount and nothing more to discuss. If you say there is a fixed amount, up to ten is obvious to me. Eleven...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new question. He explains which cases are already clear to him, and this sets up his real question about eleven לוג, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי works through both sides of the dispute. On the view that there is no fixed amount, the wine can always be split into standard portions with the extra going to נדבה, so there is no question. On the view that there is a fixed amount, he says everything up to ten לוג is already clear, so his doubt starts only at eleven.
